claims.statement: `src/docs.json` owns Mintlify navigation, redirects, and OpenAPI configuration independently from `DocumentationBuilder`, which emits authored source families into build routes; therefore emitting a source page does not itself add a navigation entry.

The builder emits language-specific OSS routes for Python and JavaScript, but emits OpenWiki and Deep Agents Code once at unversioned OSS paths; docs.json presents the same OpenWiki routes in both Build language dropdowns.
Managed Deep Agents source files emit Python and JavaScript variants, while unversioned Managed Deep Agents URLs redirect to the Python variant.
docs.json configures Agent Server, Control Plane, and LangSmith REST OpenAPI surfaces; Mintlify generates their endpoint pages at deployment rather than from authored MDX.
The builder rejects source-tree symlinks and source files that resolve outside the collection root.

The LangSmith REST OpenAPI file is a committed, post-processed input: the processor allow-lists the live LangSmith host, hides fleet/internal operations and configured health paths, assigns and orders tag groups, and normalizes visible operation titles before writing `src/langsmith/langsmith-platform-openapi.json`.

The daily OpenAPI refresh workflow runs the processor, makes no commit when the committed specification is unchanged, and appends changes to an existing `chore/refresh-langsmith-openapi` pull request so only one refresh PR remains open.

Markdown snippets are emitted at their source-relative path plus Python and JavaScript copies; language-targeted MDX imports are rewritten to the matching copy, while JSX and TSX snippet components remain shared.

Runnable documentation examples are owned by `src/code-samples/`: `make test-code-samples` executes them, while `make code-snippets` extracts marked regions into `src/code-samples-generated/` and renders generated MDX below `src/snippets/code-samples/`.

`src/` is the authored documentation input and `build/` is disposable Mintlify deployment output: `DocumentationBuilder.build_all()` deletes and recreates the build directory, while the production workflow builds it before publishing the nested output to the `prod` branch.

The `docs` console script exposes the pipeline CLI; `docs dev` performs an initial build unless skipped, watches `src/`, and serves `build/` through `mint dev`, failing before startup when the initial build fails.

Markdown preprocessing resolves `@[...]` references, adds UTM parameters to LangSmith CTA links, and selects only the target-language `:::python` or `:::js` conditional blocks while preserving unsupported conditional labels.
`packages.yml` is package metadata consumed by generated integration surfaces; the partner-package generator writes the Python provider overview, and CI rejects manual changes to that generated page.
The weekly package-download workflow updates package metadata, regenerates the provider overview and integration-download snippets, and creates a PR only when those tracked generated outputs changed.

The main CI workflow calls reusable test, lint, and link-validation workflows and separately checks cross-references and generated files; the reusable link workflow validates built links with anchors and the Agent Server OpenAPI specification.
The Monday integration-repository workflow runs the checker with `--write` and creates or appends changes only to the standing `chore/dead-integration-repos` draft pull request.

For a dead third-party GitHub home, the integration-repository checker can adopt a live third-party replacement evidenced by PyPI, npm, or external documentation, but retains live GitLab, partner-documentation, and first-party alternatives for attention; it delists only when no live alternate exists and removes associated listing surfaces.

`scripts/refresh_integration_downloads.py` combines hosted integration-page frontmatter with third-party rows from `scripts/data/integration_external_docs.yaml`; third-party names link to their validated external `docs_url` rather than a hosted guide, and CI checks the allowed URL schemes.
Scoped entries in `pipeline/preprocessors/link_map.py` are the authority used to resolve `@[...]` references; unresolved symbols are logged and left literal rather than receiving a guessed URL.
The main CI workflow cancels an in-progress run for the same workflow and Git ref when a newer push arrives, while retaining distinct jobs for merge-conflict and external-document URL validation.

A code sample's snippet markers deterministically own its display MDX: `rag-deep.py` marks `rag-deep-index-py`, the extractor removes marked non-display regions while emitting an intermediate, and the MDX generator writes that snippet id as `src/snippets/code-samples/rag-deep-index-py.mdx`.

The create-agent guide displays derived MDX from a runnable source: `create-an-agent.mdx` imports `create-agent-py.mdx`, which is extracted from a marked region in `src/code-samples/langsmith/create-an-agent.py`; the source runs the SDK against a loopback fixture and asserts the creation and retrieval requests without creating a live agent.

Source-directory ownership and reader-facing navigation labels are intentionally independent: navigation products and menus can draw from multiple source directories, so contributors must locate the page owner by directory and discoverability by `src/docs.json`.

The weekly changelog workflow proposes Cloud and Fleet updates from a Monday-to-Monday window of merged `feat` and `fix` langchainplus pull requests, writes the two committed changelog targets only in write mode, and keeps flag-gated work in the encrypted `scripts/.changelog_held.json.enc` ledger until rollout.

`docs-release-watch` is a separately deployable Managed Deep Agent that covers OpenWiki and three Deep Agents variants; for eligible releases published 7–30 days ago it compares source changes to the configured documentation boundary and creates one Linear DOC ticket and one draft PR per feature, with coverage extended through a registry entry, matching skill, schedule prompt, and redeploy.
